en deltager.explanation: "En deltager" means "a participant". It comes from the verb "at deltage" (to take part). To say which event someone took part in, use "i" (in) after it: "en deltager i kurset" (a participant in the course).

en deltagerliste.explanation: "En deltagerliste" means "a list of participants". It is built from "en deltager" (a participant) and "en liste" (a list). The part "liste" is also in "en indkøbsliste" (a shopping list).

en demonstration.explanation: "En demonstration" means "a demonstration". When a crowd gathers or marches to show publicly what it wants, use it for the event: "Der var en demonstration i går" (There was a demonstration yesterday). When someone shows how a machine works, use it for the showing: "Vi fik en demonstration af maskinen" (We were given a demonstration of the machine).

en deodorant.explanation: "En deodorant" means "a deodorant". To say you have or use deodorant in general, leave out "en": "Har du deodorant?" (Do you have deodorant?).

en depression.explanation: "En depression" means "a depression". To describe a person who has one, use the adjective "deprimeret" (depressed): "Han er deprimeret" (He is depressed).

en designer.explanation: "En designer" means "a designer". To say what kind of designer someone is, put a word before it: "en grafisk designer" (a graphic designer).

en dessert.explanation: "En dessert" means "a dessert". To ask what the dessert will be, use "til" (for): "Hvad skal vi have til dessert?" (What are we having for dessert?). Do not mix it up with "en ørken" (a desert): "Sahara er en ørken" (The Sahara is a desert).

en destination.explanation: "En destination" means "a destination". To say you arrive there, use "at nå" (to reach) before it: "Vi nåede vores destination sent om aftenen" (We reached our destination late in the evening).

en detalje.explanation: "En detalje" means "a detail". To say you do something in full detail, use "i detaljer" (in detail) after the verb: "Hun forklarede alt i detaljer" (She explained everything in detail).

en detektiv.explanation: "En detektiv" means "a detective". To talk about a detective who works for private clients, add "privat" at the start: "en privatdetektiv" (a private detective).

en detektor.explanation: "En detektor" means "a detector". To name a detector for one kind of thing, put that thing before it: "en metaldetektor" (a metal detector). Do not mix it up with "en detektiv" (a detective): "Detektiven fandt nøglen" (The detective found the key).

en diagnose.explanation: "En diagnose" means "a diagnosis". To say a doctor makes one, use "at stille" (to put) before it: "Lægen stillede en diagnose" (The doctor made a diagnosis).

en dialekt.explanation: "En dialekt" means "a dialect". Denmark has regional dialects such as "sønderjysk" (the dialect of South Jutland) and "bornholmsk" (the dialect of Bornholm).

en dialog.explanation: "En dialog" means "a dialogue". English speakers should note the spelling: Danish has no "ue" at the end. To say two sides talk openly with each other, use "at føre" (to hold): "Politikerne vil føre en dialog med borgerne" (The politicians want to hold a dialogue with the citizens).

en diamant.explanation: "En diamant" means "a diamond". To talk about jewelry, use the compound "en diamantring" (a diamond ring). In a card game, the suit is called "ruder" (diamonds) instead: "Hun har ruder es" (She has the ace of diamonds).

en diameter.explanation: "En diameter" means "a diameter". Do not mix it up with "en radius" (a radius), which is half as long: "Cirklen har en radius på fem centimeter, så diameteren er ti" (The circle has a radius of five centimeters, so the diameter is ten).

en digter.explanation: "En digter" means "a poet". It comes from the verb "at digte" (to write poetry): "Han digter om natten" (He writes poetry at night).

en digtsamling.explanation: "En digtsamling" means "a poetry collection". It is built from "et digt" (a poem) and "en samling" (a collection). The part "samling" is also in "en frimærkesamling" (a stamp collection).

en diktat.explanation: "En diktat" means "a dictation". It comes from the verb "at diktere" (to dictate): "Chefen dikterer et brev" (The boss dictates a letter).

en diktator.explanation: "En diktator" means "a dictator". To name the kind of country he rules, use "et diktatur" (a dictatorship): "Landet er et diktatur" (The country is a dictatorship).

en dimension.explanation: "En dimension" means "a dimension". To talk about space, use "i tre dimensioner" (in three dimensions): "et billede i tre dimensioner" (a picture in three dimensions). To say something adds a new side to a matter, use it as well: "Det giver sagen en ny dimension" (That gives the matter a new dimension).

en diplomat.explanation: "En diplomat" means "a diplomat". To describe a tactful person in daily life, use it too: "Hun er en rigtig diplomat" (She is a real diplomat). The adjective is "diplomatisk" (diplomatic): "Det var et diplomatisk svar" (That was a diplomatic answer).

en direktør.explanation: "En direktør" means "a director / CEO". To say CEO precisely, add "administrerende" (managing): "Hun er administrerende direktør i et stort firma" (She is the managing director of a large company).

en dirigent.explanation: "En dirigent" means "a conductor". Do not mix it up with "en konduktør" (a ticket inspector on a train): "Konduktøren tjekker billetterne" (The ticket inspector checks the tickets). At a meeting, "en dirigent" is also the person who chairs it: "Vi skal vælge en dirigent til generalforsamlingen" (We need to choose a chair for the general meeting).

en disharmoni.explanation: "En disharmoni" means "a discord". It is built from "dis-" and "en harmoni" (a harmony), so it is the opposite. To say that notes in music clash, use it for the sound: "Akkorden var en disharmoni" (The chord was a discord).
